objective: Show two different frames in a known order inside one connection, and confirm the device renders them in that order. Nothing more.

target.pairing_precheck: authenticated exact target required before any socket is created

transport.one_controller_rule: the Android app must be disconnected for the whole run

operation.shape: one connection; per frame send stock-observed preamble A, preamble B, then the image packet; read one ACK; then the next frame; then close
operation.semantic_evidence: capture2 btsnoop b373607316094b0fd529f3354ee379abb6645e89ab0b2c06ce865064428dbc9c: the official app sends 41 image packets inside ONE open serial session with no reconnect between frames, each preceded by preamble frames and each answered by exactly one ACK (41/41, none missing).

application_tx_sequence.name: close
application_tx_sequence.note: local socket close; no further traffic

a.content: 3x3 white block in the top-left corner, rows 0-2 columns 0-2

b.content: 3x3 white block in the bottom-right corner, rows 13-15 columns 13-15

source_frames.why_these: Opposite corners are unmistakable at a glance and cannot be confused with each other, so the operator can report the render order without measuring anything. M6.4 already proved top-left/bottom-right geometry, so a wrong order cannot be explained away as a flip.

budgets.derivation: Inter-frame delay is the stock median gap (1.013 s). Stock sustained a 148 ms minimum gap, so 1000 ms is roughly 7x more conservative than demonstrated. ACK timeout is ~31x the slowest observed stock ACK (160.9 ms; median 45.6 ms).

expected_observations.transport: one connection, six application packets, two wrapped 0x44 ACKs, clean local close
expected_observations.physical: top-left block appears first, then about one second later the bottom-right block replaces it
expected_observations.ack_payload: not validated against any fixed value; observed successful payloads so far are 0x12, 0x75 and 0xF0, so the byte is recorded, not asserted

persistence_analysis.basis: M6.4 power cycle returned the unit to stock software and the default clock
persistence_analysis.not_claimed: absence of any non-volatile write; this experiment does not test that and must not be cited as evidence for it
persistence_analysis.new_persistence_risk_vs_m6: none identified: the same command and packet shape already accepted in M5/M6, sent twice instead of once, with no new command id, no save/publish/upload command and no gallery interaction

stop_immediately_on: unexpected target identity or pairing precheck failure
an ACK that is not exactly one 10-byte wrapped 0x44 frame
any send that does not complete in full
any conflicting controller observed on the link
any device behaviour outside the expected observations, including a stock page takeover
stop_policy.on_ambiguous_outcome: stop, preserve the Host diagnostics record, and report. Do NOT resend either frame, do not reconnect, and do not power-cycle to 'clear' state before the result is recorded.
stop_policy.recovery: operator-initiated only; a power cycle is permitted only after the outcome has been recorded

authority.note: This manifest is a prepared proposal. It grants nothing. It becomes executable only when the operator grants authority for this exact experiment id, and that grant covers this two-frame sequence once - not a loop, not a rate increase, and not continuous display.
authority.grant_scope: this exact experiment id, one execution of the two-frame sequence at the stated budgets. Not a loop, not a rate increase, not continuous display.

explicitly_out_of_scope: any rate above the stated inter-frame delay
removing or reordering the stock-observed preambles
keeping the connection open beyond this sequence
driving the display from the M9 activity collector

result.note: Every budget in this manifest was met exactly. Ordered ACKs prove the device accepted frame A then frame B on one connection. They do NOT prove render order; that needs the operator's observation.

findings.statement: The exact unit accepts two different image frames inside one connection, each answered by its own wrapped 0x44 ACK, with no reconnect between them. 6/6 packets and 142/142 bytes were sent, and the socket closed cleanly.
findings.not_claimed: Render order, rendering at all, and any rate above the 1000 ms inter-frame delay used here.

findings.statement: The two ACKs in this single session were 0xE5 and 0x33, both different from each other and from the previously observed 0x12, 0x75 and 0xF0. This further supports that the wrapped 0x44 ACK payload byte is not a success constant.
findings.not_claimed: Any semantic meaning for the byte, including that it is a counter or sequence.
